title: Privacy Policy
summary: How Next Best Action collects, uses and protects personal information, including health information, and the choices and rights you have. This is a draft prepared for a proof-of-concept application and must be reviewed by qualified legal and privacy counsel before production use.

sections.heading: 1. Who we are and how to contact us

blocks.p: Next Best Action is a software platform that helps healthcare organisations decide the next useful communication with a patient or a healthcare professional. It is operated by {{controller_name}}, {{controller_address}} ("we", "us").

For the personal information described in this policy, the operator acts as the controller unless a customer organisation that deploys the platform determines the purposes of processing, in which case that organisation is the controller and we act on its instructions. Which of these applies is to be confirmed for each deployment.

head: Contact
Details
rows: {{privacy_email}}, or Data & privacy in your account

blocks.p: This policy covers the Next Best Action web application: the public pages, account sign-up and sign-in, the patient and healthcare-professional portals, and the workspaces used by care managers, medical representatives, compliance reviewers and administrators.

blocks.note: This is a proof-of-concept. The patient and healthcare-professional records in the application are synthetic (invented). When you create a patient or healthcare-professional account, your account is linked to a synthetic record, which is then shown under your name. The medications, prescription fills and engagement history in that record are not yours. Your own account details (name, email, date of birth, country, password and consent choices) are real and are handled as described here.

blocks.p: We do not collect your postal address, phone number, payment details, precise location, or any biometric data. We do not use analytics, advertising or tracking technologies (see the Cookie Policy).

sections.heading: 4. Date of birth, age and minors

blocks.p: We ask for your date of birth to confirm eligibility. From it, and from your country (and US state), the application works out on its own server whether you are an adult where you live. The age of adulthood is configured per jurisdiction; it is 18 unless a jurisdiction's rule differs.

list: Professional accounts are available only to adults.

People under the age of adulthood may create a patient account; the account is marked as belonging to a minor, so it can be handled with additional care. Additional requirements, such as consent from a parent or guardian, are not yet implemented and would be added before the service is offered to minors in production.
Your full date of birth is not shown to other users. Administrators see only whether an account belongs to an adult, a minor, or someone whose age is not recorded.

blocks.review: Age thresholds, minors' processing and any parental-consent requirements must be confirmed per jurisdiction by counsel.

list: To create and secure your account, verify your email, and sign you in.
To onboard healthcare professionals and staff by invitation, and to show who invited whom.
To give each person access only to the information their role and assignments allow.
For patients: to show you your medications and messages, to respect your contact and sharing choices, and to support medication adherence.
To generate recommendations for the next useful communication (see section 9) and to let staff review, edit, approve or reject them.
To keep a record of security-relevant and governance actions, detect misuse, and limit repeated sign-in or verification attempts.
To answer your privacy requests and keep a record of your choices.

blocks.p: We do not sell personal information, and we do not use it for advertising or share it for cross-context behavioural advertising.
Where the GDPR or UK GDPR applies, we rely on the following bases. They are proposed and are to be confirmed by counsel for each deployment.

blocks.review: Legal bases, including whether health information is processed on explicit consent or another Article 9 condition (for example the provision of health or social care), must be confirmed by counsel.

blocks.p: Information about medications, prescription fills and adherence is health information and is treated as highly sensitive. In the application:

list: Patients see only their own record, without internal risk scores.
Care managers see only the patients assigned to them; medical representatives see no patient information.
Healthcare professionals see adherence only for their own patients who have consented to sharing it.
Compliance reviewers see recommendation outcomes without the identity of the person concerned, and the audit log with emails and record identifiers masked.
Every view of a full patient profile is recorded in the audit log.
Verification and invitation emails contain no health information.

blocks.p: Whether the US Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) applies depends on how the platform is operated (for example, on behalf of a covered entity under a business associate agreement). That determination has not been made and is to be confirmed. This policy does not state that HIPAA does or does not apply.

For healthcare professionals, care managers, medical representatives, compliance reviewers and administrators we process account and invitation information, assignments, the actions they take in the application (which are audited), and, for healthcare professionals, the professional record and messages linked to their account. Professional roles are granted only by an authorised invitation, and a professional's verified status shows that they completed it.
The application analyses information about patients and healthcare professionals to suggest the next useful communication. This is profiling. Specifically it:

list: calculates adherence measures from prescription fills and a risk score from them;
estimates, using statistical models trained on past outcomes, how likely a person is to respond to each possible message and channel;
checks every option against fixed rules (content approval, consent per channel, contact limits) that models cannot override;
ranks the remaining options and explains its choice in plain language;
drafts the message wording from approved content (by templates; an external language model is not used unless explicitly enabled).

blocks.p: A person reviews every recommendation before anything is sent, and can edit, reject or approve it. The application does not make clinical decisions, and it does not take any decision that produces legal effects or similarly significantly affects you solely by automated means. Recommendations are communication suggestions; healthcare professionals remain responsible for clinical decisions.
You can object to this processing or ask about it through a privacy request (section 15).

blocks.p: Security measures in the application include: passwords stored only as salted hashes; one-time codes for email verification; sessions held server-side in a cookie that scripts cannot read; protection against cross-site request forgery; limits on repeated sign-in, sign-up and verification attempts; access by role and assignment checked on the server for every request; and an append-only audit log. No security measure is perfect.
If a breach of personal information occurs, we will assess it and notify the affected people and authorities where the law requires. A documented breach-response procedure is to be defined.

blocks.review: Encryption of stored data, infrastructure security and the breach-response procedure are to be confirmed before production; this policy makes no claim about them.

blocks.p: Depending on where you live, you may have the right to:

list: access the personal information we hold about you;
have inaccurate information corrected;
have your information deleted;
restrict or object to certain processing, including profiling;
receive your information in a portable format;
withdraw consent at any time, without affecting processing that happened before;
not be discriminated against for exercising your rights;
complain to a data protection or other supervisory authority (in the EU/EEA, the authority where you live or work, or where an issue arose).

blocks.p: Residents of some US states, including California, have rights under state privacy laws, such as to know, correct and delete personal information and to limit the use of sensitive personal information. We do not sell or share personal information for cross-context behavioural advertising, so opt-out controls for those uses are not needed. Which state laws apply depends on the operator and is to be confirmed.

Signed in, open Data & privacy. You can download a copy of your account and portal data straight away, withdraw consent, and submit a request (access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, objection or another question). A request is reviewed by a person; you can see its status in Data & privacy. We aim to respond within {{response_days}} days, and may need to verify your identity.
You can also write to {{privacy_email}}.

We will publish any change as a new version with a new effective date. Earlier versions remain available. When a change is significant, we will ask you to review and accept the new version before you continue to use the application.
